- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially after spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), particularly if recent prices are trending down; add 3–5% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope and adjust downward by 2–4% per day of negative sentiment.
- Avoid over-optimism after sharp price spikes; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x the 14-day moving average unless sentiment remains bullish.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early correction after initial spike, reduce forecast by 3–5% in the first 5 days of the forecast window.
